title: POC: INT8/FP8 weekly bakeoff review
summary: Weekly POC sync to review the bakeoff results between INT8 and FP8 variants, align on observed quality regressions, confirm latency/throughput deltas, and agree next steps for tuning and an e2e latency benchmark. Customer raised VPC and KMS concerns; Redwood to send additional security docs and run a dedicated capacity cost estimate.
next_steps: Diego to run 2048 token end-to-end latency benchmark with 4x batch profiles and share results (due 2026-03-16)
Maya to send dedicated capacity pricing and pilot SOW options (due 2026-03-14)
Sara to confirm top 300 prompts for focused quality eval and share scoring rubric (due 2026-03-15)
Redwood Security (Evelyn) to book an intro with BlueLeaf security team for VPC/KMS review (target 2026-03-19)
action_items: Diego Ramos - rerun quant blend (INT8 baseline vs FP8 blend) with temperature 0.7 and stop tokens, produce per-prompt diffs + aggregate SNR (due 2026-03-16)
Maya Patel - email pricing and Dedicated capacity SOW + note on burst policies (due 2026-03-14)
Sara Kim - share canonical prompt set (300) and baseline outputs for quality gating (due 2026-03-15)
Evelyn Cho - schedule security deep-dive and attach SOC2 section relevant to data residency (due 2026-03-19)
Tom Alvarez - provide a short note on current infra limits and target qps for e2e test (due 2026-03-15)
transcript:
Header: Date: 2026-03-12 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48m
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Evelyn Cho (Redwood CSM); Sara Kim, Tom Alvarez, Priya Shah, Jared Lin (BlueLeaf)

00:00 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining — we wanted to run through the weekly bakeoff results for the quantization pilot, right. quick agenda, results, quality deltas, perf numbers, and next steps.
00:18 Sara: yep thanks, excited to see. we did a first pass over customer-facing prompts and saw some weird hallucinations in int8 on a handful, so we want to understand whether it's tuning or intrinsic.
00:35 Diego: got it. so we ran three variants: full-fp16 baseline, int8 symmetric quant, and an fp8 mixed-blend from the compiler. side note, some labels in our internal sheet got swapped — sorry about that — the "blend" column was shifted by one row for a subset.
00:58 Priya: oh yeah we noticed that too, a couple of mismatched rows. but the aggregated tables you sent looked ok after Diego fixed them?
01:06 Diego: yeah that was fixed v quickly, but thanks for the flag. high level numbers: token throughput for int8 improved about 2.7x vs fp16 at batch 8 on the A100-ish profile; fp8 got 3.1x. p50 latency delta was ~22% lower for fp8 vs fp16 and int8 was ~18%. tail latency p95 for int8 showed more variance, about +12% relative to fp16 in one of our runs.
01:36 Tom: can you repeat the p95 comment? we worry about spikes — production is scary there.
01:40 Diego: sure. in the mixed workload run with variable sequence lengths we saw int8 p95 go up on one node when the kv-cache got warmed concurrently; suspect fewer stable kernels for cached ops in int8 path. fp8 maintained a more consistent tail, likely because our FP8 kernel fallback path keeps some fp16 ops for attention.
02:05 Sara: hmm ok. qualitatively, the errors we flagged were: wrong dosages in a guideline answer, and one case where the model hallucinated a nonexistent ICD code. are those the type of failures you saw in the diff report?
02:18 Diego: yes those exact prompts show bigger delta in BLEU-ish scoring and F1 on entity extraction. for the dosage case int8 had a substitution error in the numeric generation token, fp8 preserved it in most runs. but across the whole 300 prompt set the average semantic score drop for int8 was ~3.4% vs baseline, fp8 was ~1.1%.
02:45 Priya: 3.4% is a blocker for clinical — we need under 1% for critical content. is there a known knob to reduce that?
02:52 Diego: a few levers: higher calibration bits (e.g., per-channel quantization), selective layer keep-in-fp16 for sensitive heads, or temperature/prompt-engineering heuristics. there's also a pipeline-level option we call "sensitivity gate" where we run a cheap verifier for numeric tokens.
03:14 Jared: from security side — any change in model outputs impact audit logs or can the verifier be run within our VPC? we can't send PHI out.
03:23 Evelyn: yes, good point. Redwood Private supports running the verifier inside the customer's VPC and we can wire KMS for key management; we'll pair you with the security docs after this call.
03:35 Sara: great. on perf, the throughput gains are attractive but not if we lose critical content. what about rollback strategies?
03:42 Maya: we recommend a hybrid rollout: sample-based routing where 90% goes to quant variant and 10% to fp16 golden path for high-risk prompt classes until we clear gating. also automated fallback on verifier fail.
03:56 Tom: how intrusive is the sampling routing in our infra? that needs to sit in the app layer ideally.
04:03 Diego: it can be RG in the runtime — we support route policies by prompt tag or token patterns, but you can also implement client-side sampling. runtime approach gives you better metrics and cheaper cross-checking since you avoid double egress.
04:27 Priya: can you explain the "sensitivity gate" flow again?
04:31 Diego: sure — it's basically a small model or set of heuristics that checks for critical tokens (numbers, ICD, dosages) and flags a reroute to the fp16 path if confidence is low or token patterns look risky. cheap to run, adds a few ms.
04:48 Sara: a few ms might be okay if it prevents bad outputs. what was the end-to-end latency in your reported benchmarks?
04:55 Diego: our synthetic per-request (no network) p50s were 85ms fp16 baseline, 48ms int8, 42ms fp8 at batch 8. when we add e2e networking and the KV warm path we predicted 120ms fp16, ~68ms int8, ~61ms fp8 — these are estimates, we need the e2e run to confirm.
05:22 Tom: those numbers look promising. we have a hard SLO of 100ms p50 for our interactive product, so fp8 seems within range; int8 might be borderline in tail scenarios.
05:34 Diego: agreed. also note cost delta — int8 reduced token cost by ~45% vs fp16, fp8 ~52% in our pricing sim.
05:44 Priya: can you share the pricing sim spreadsheet?
05:47 Maya: yes we'll share. it's in the links we just posted.
05:52 Sara: about the hallucination cases, is that likely model-architecture sensitive (i.e., some models degrade more with quant) or purely quant hyperparams?
05:59 Diego: both. certain architectures are more resilient; we picked your target open model family that tends to be moderately robust. quant hyperparams matter a lot — per-channel vs per-tensor, activation clipping, and renormalization during calibration. we recommend per-channel for sensitive deployments.
06:20 Priya: how much extra cost/complexity does per-channel add?
06:24 Diego: slightly more memory overhead and calibration time; runtime perf delta is marginal. in our experience it's worth it when you care about token-level fidelity.
06:36 Sara: ok. on the action items, can we ask for a focused re-run on the 12 prompts that failed with int8 and see whether per-channel or the sensitivity gate fixes them?
06:45 Diego: absolutely. we'll do a micro-run toggling per-channel, keep-layers, and the gate.
06:51 Tom: and please include a run where the kv-cache is under write load as that seemed to cause the tail blips.
06:58 Diego: noted.
07:02 Maya: for the next call we'll want updated diffs and also an e2e latency test that simulates your infra — Tom, can you share a small test harness or endpoint info?
07:11 Tom: yes I'll send a small harness and a target qps profile.
07:15 Priya: on compliance — any implications for logs retention when running Dedicated?
07:19 Evelyn: Dedicated keeps per-request traces under your tenancy and we can TTL or redact logs per your policy. we'll include the SOC2 excerpt in the follow-up.
07:28 Sara: any competitors we should be worried about? some teams mentioned Huggin Face managed infra and Vertex endpoints — they both offer quant but without this fine-grained gate/fallback story.
07:40 Maya: yes, we talked briefly about that. our differentiation is the runtime-level routing and the cost/latency visibility — console will show token-level breakdowns so you can see where regressions happen.
07:52 Jared: last question from security: how do you handle KMS rotation without interrupting in-flight inference?
07:59 Evelyn: we use key-wrapping and can rotate keys with a staged rollout; the runtime keeps a short-lived wrapping key so in-flight requests are unaffected. we'll include the rotation diagram in the security deck.
08:14 Maya: okay let's recap the plan and owners — Diego runs micro-diff on the 12 flagged prompts with per-channel and sensitivity gate and kv-cache load (due 3/16). Maya sends pricing and SOW (due 3/14). Evelyn schedules security deep-dive (target 3/19). Sara shares prompt set and Tom shares harness (due 3/15).
08:40 Sara: sounds good. thanks everyone.
08:44 Maya: thanks — we'll follow up in email with the artifacts and a short summary.

[meeting end]
